title: Regional evacuation drill: progressive load-shed + circuit-breaker validation
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: validate that Redwood’s multi-region failover and runtime load-shedding strategies preserve customer-facing SLOs during realistic region loss and GPU pool exhaustion events. We will run a staged chaos drill that exercises: (1) simulated full-region evacuation, (2) controlled GPU pool eviction/CPU fallback, and (3) dependency blackholes for storage and auth. The experiment will verify circuit-breaker behavior, progressive shedding thresholds, routing fallbacks, and automated rollbacks. Deliverables: chaos harness scripts, dashboards for SLO/ops metrics, runbook updates for production drills, and a postmortem with remediation items.
acceptance_criteria: No more than 2% increase in overall error-rate beyond baseline for P99 tail traffic across targeted routes during staged experiments
99th-percentile latency for critical routes must remain under SLO (500ms) when routed to degraded mode; if not, automatic rollback triggers successfully
Progressive load-shedding policy must drop lowest-priority requests first and preserve high-priority/enterprise traffic (verified by token-level traces)
Circuit-breaker trips should prevent cascading failures: downstream DB/kv blackholes must not cause full-service outage
Runbook and playbook committed: step-by-step drill procedure, rollback commands, and post-drill monitoring checklist
comments: 2026-03-11: Design review with PM Priya Kapoor and SRE lead Sven Jorgensen. Agreed on 3-phase drill: small staging run, broad staging run with synthetic traffic, and a limited production window (business hours only).

2026-03-12: Prototype scripts added in chaos-sims repo (PR #512). Implementation uses k8s taints+pod disruption budgets to emulate GPU eviction and iptables rules to simulate dependency blackholes in staging clusters.

2026-03-13: Initial staging run (canary subset) notes: GPU eviction caused KV cache cold starts increasing 95p latency temporarily; CPU fallback model kept 99p under target for enterprise traffic but non-enterprise paths saw elevated token costs. Added metric: per-token-cost delta for degraded mode.

2026-03-14: PM requested adding token-level priority tagging to ensure load-shedding preserves enterprise tokens. Added follow-up sub-issue ENG-15810 to instrument token-priority propagation in the proxy layer.
Post-run action: update autoscaler policies to cap concurrent prefix warms during region failover and add a 30s KV warmup grace period in routing logic.
